newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Hasan says Bre-X can sell Busang stake.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Hasan says Bre-X can sell Busang stake.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd of Canada is free to sell its 45 percent stake in the huge Busang gold find without offering the right of first refusal to its Indonesian partners, Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, an Indonesian Bre-X partner, said Tuesday.
"There's no need for our permission," Hasan said in a telephone interview.

He was commenting on a statement by Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh that the company's stake in Busang, believed to be one of the world's biggest gold deposits, was held through its wholly-owned Dutch subsidiary.
"It's just like selling Dutch shares in Amsterdam," Hasan said. "It's okay. There's no need for our permission."
He added that the right of first refusal applied only to locally incorporated companies.
"If the company is locally incorporated, ...yes. It is a standard article of corporation," he said.
Hasan heads the Nusamba group, which has 50 percent stakes in PT Askatindo Karya Minerals and PT Amsya Lyna, which have a combined 30 percent share in the richest parts of Busang.

Under an agreement approved by the Indonesian government, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc. will hold a 15 percent stake in Busang and the remaining 10 percent will be held by the Indonesian government.
